summary: Sidecar checkpointer causing ephemeral GPU evictions, sustained autoscaler lag and throughput collapse
description:
Issue summary:
A customer on a Dedicated pool (NimbusDocs, prod-us-east) reported a sustained throughput collapse over a 90-minute window. Investigation shows repeated ephemeral GPU evictions and node reprovisioning correlated with a sidecar checkpointer process that spikes host I/O and triggers preemption signals in the GPU scheduler.

Impact:
- Customer traffic experienced p99 latency increases from ~120ms to 3.2s and 5xxs for ~1.5 hours.
- Autoscaler failed to stabilize: repeated node adds then immediate evictions created capacity thrash and billing surprise for the customer.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) serving production routes for NimbusDocs.
- Region: us-east-1.
- Affected model routes: gpt-3.5-large, redwood-optimized-7b.

Timeline / Observed behavior:
- 2026-03-12 16:05 UTC: Customer opened high-latency alert (p99 > 2s).
- 16:07 UTC: Support acknowledged and escalated to SRE.
- 16:15–16:55 UTC: Event storm — repeated GPU detach/attach logs on 3 nodes.
- 16:30 UTC: Autoscaler triggered two scale-ups; new nodes provisioned but evicted within 2–4 minutes.
- 16:40 UTC: Monitoring shows host-side I/O saturation and dd-agent traces with long fsyncs from /var/lib/sidecar-checkpointer.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1. Deploy long-context chat sessions to dedicated pool with heavy periodic snapshotting enabled in customer container.
2. Sidecar checkpointer performs large file writes and fsync bursts (every ~10–20s) during peak.
3. Host FIO/IOPS spike induces GPU preemption in our runtime, batch queues stall, and autoscaler misreads capacity signals.

Logs & metrics (representative):
- runtime-node-42: gpu.detach: timestamp 2026-03-12T16:22:11Z; reason: host-io-timeout
- node-42 dd-agent: fsync latency 1.2s -> 3.6s spikes around 16:20–16:35 UTC
- autoscaler: scale-up node-83 provisioned 16:27; healthcheck fail 16:30 (evicted)
- monitoring: NVLINK retries and kernel nvlink warnings coincident with fsync spikes

Hypothesis:
The sidecar checkpointer (customer container process) is performing frequent large synchronous disk flushes that push host I/O into stall states. Our serving runtime detects prolonged device/service stalls and emits preemptive GPU detach for safety, which triggers the autoscaler to provision replacement nodes. The short life of replacements plus recurring I/O spikes cause thrash and apparent noisy-neighbor symptoms inside a dedicated pool.

Initial mitigations applied:
- 2026-03-12 17:00 UTC: Temporarily tainted nodes exhibiting heavy fsyncs to stop new placements to affected hosts.
- 17:12 UTC: Applied a soft-cap on eviction threshold to allow existing in-flight batches to drain instead of immediate detach (reduced customer 5xxs).
- 17:25 UTC: Support asked customer to disable sidecar checkpoint frequency; customer applied conservative snapshot schedule as temporary workaround.

Next steps / proposed remediation:
- SRE: deploy a background I/O watchdog that demotes scheduling priority of sidecar processes or rate-limits fsync bursts on dedicated hosts.
- Runtime: add a transient backoff to avoid immediate GPU detach for single short IO-induced stalls (PR drafted).
- Product/Customer success: review recommended sidecar checkpoint config for dedicated customers and add guidance to runbooks.
- Schedule a targeted postmortem and a change to autoscaler heuristic to detect repeated rapid evictions as a signal to pause new provisioning.

Links:
- Dashboards: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/ops/dedicated/gpu-evictions?pool=nimbusdocs
- Logs (sample): https://logs.redwood.internal/query?q=node-42+fsync
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4689
investigation_notes: Root_cause_hypothesis: Sidecar checkpointer synchronous fsync bursts -> host I/O saturation -> runtime GPU preemption -> autoscaler thrash. Evidence: correlated fsync spikes and GPU detach logs; eviction timing lines up with checkpointer cron; tainting nodes stopped new placements and reduced error rate. Next: add host-level IO cgroup limits or recommend off-host checkpointing for heavy snapshot workloads.

2026-03-12 17:05 - SRE (Sophie Chen): Taunted nodes showing high fsyncs; applied node taints to prevent new allocations. Requesting customer to pause sidecar checkpoint frequency.

resolution: Mitigations in progress: nodes tainted to prevent new placements, soft eviction threshold applied, customer reduced checkpoint frequency. Patch PR opened to soften immediate GPU detach and autoscaler heuristic update in review. Postmortem scheduled and runbook updates planned.
next_steps: (1) Merge runtime PR and roll out canary for autoscaler heuristic update. (2) Implement host-level IO controls for sidecars on dedicated pools. (3) Update customer onboarding docs with recommended checkpoint schedules and off-host snapshot patterns.
